title: plugins: a queue sharing recipient still revokes grants on a member-table outage, because the queue expander answers "nobody" for every consumer; refuse for the sharing-grant pass and the approver slate (ADR-0142 amendment first)
body:
domain:server#3 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmQJdgarUjPLNgFBY67

Filing gate: ③ open question 1 of the #29503 dev (os-dev-report `6588119628`, site 4), ruled by the seat (`6588178193`): A on PR #29602, and direction B filed here. Filed by `domain:server` seat 3. ⛔ Not a claim. Suggested-grade: p2 (same defect class as #29362 / #29503: on an outage, a recompute revokes share grants it should keep).

## What happens

`packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/ownership-queue-service.ts` catches any member-table read failure during expansion, warns "contributes nobody until it can", and answers `[]` (`isMember` answers `false`). The file header declares that posture: "a failed read of a member table contributes nobody for that specification (fail closed for every admission that reads it)". ADR-0142 itself does not declare it. D2 says "an empty expansion is a fact, not a fault". D5 says a failed read during assignment "leaves the row as it was … and logs at warn".

After PR #29602 (#29503), every other sharing and approvals recipient read refuses on a failed read. The queue expander is the last one that answers "nobody". So a `queue` sharing recipient (ADR-0142 D7) is still diffed against a set that is missing its members on an outage, through reconcile (`revokeRuleGrantsForRetiredRecipients`) and through the per-user recompute via `isMember`, and its grants are revoked. The approver slate (D6) can likewise route to a shrunk set. Source reading, not reproduced through a public door.

## Wanted (direction ruled B)

1. **ADR-0142 amendment first** (a governed path; its own PR, approved by `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` before code relies on it). It adds a line to D2 saying the one expander keeps "nobody" as its fail-closed answer for admission consumers (the access path, claim admission and the assignment pool), while the sharing-recipient grant pass (D7) and the approver slate (D6) refuse on a failed read. Use the repo's ADR amendment-note recipe.
2. **Then the code:** `expandMembers` / `isMember` take the consumer's purpose, or the D6/D7 callers use a refusing variant. The access path, claim admission and the assignment pool keep failing closed, exactly as today. A refused D7 pass keeps the rule's existing grants and warns, the way #29362 isolates a rule. A refused D6 slate follows the approvals site's existing failure class from #29503.
3. Pins: a failed member read keeps queue-recipient grants on reconcile and on the per-user recompute (red on main); the access path still answers no access on the same failure (control); the approver slate refuses instead of shrinking.

Level: the D6/D7 doors narrow (a recompute that used to revoke now refuses), so expect `!`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and the full dogfood battery.

Serial: after PR #29602 merges (same files; its `holderCheck` wrapper is the seam this card changes).

Dedupe: searched `ADR-0142 queue outage`, `contributes nobody until it can`; nearest #29503. **New.**

Links back: #29503, #29602, #29362.
